title: UPI Safety Guidelines — Never Share OTP or PIN
text: NPCI's UPI safety guidelines state that your UPI PIN is equivalent to your ATM PIN and must never be shared with anyone — not with bank representatives, government officials, payment app support staff, or any third party. A UPI PIN is only required to SEND money, never to RECEIVE it. If someone asks for your UPI PIN to send you a refund or prize money, it is a scam. Similarly, your OTP (One Time Password) is a secret authentication code — no legitimate bank, payment app, or government body will ever ask you to share it over a call, SMS, or chat. Sharing your OTP immediately grants the other person full access to your account. NPCI also warns against UPI collect requests: a collect request asks you to approve a debit from your account. Legitimate refunds and prizes are credited automatically — they never require you to 'approve' or 'accept' a collect request. Never approve a collect request from an unknown UPI ID. If you receive a suspicious collect request, decline it and report it to your bank immediately.
